identity.real_world_identity_notes: Customer GT3 racing car based on the F13 M6 with the 4.4 litre twin-turbo V8, campaigned by privateer teams from 2016. Ricardo, which engineered the unit, describes a semi-automatic transverse transaxle carrying a sequential six-speed plus reverse racing gearbox in a magnesium casing, shifted by paddles.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behavior was directly observed in a guided drive with automatic clutch and shifting disabled: clutch-free move-off, six paddle-selected gears, and automatic cut and blip.
No throttle lift is required on upshifts and no manual blip on downshifts, because the drive detected automatic cut and automatic blip. This matches every other curated paddle-shift GT3 car.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.bmw-m6-gt3.20260813t155203395z-7c40ce55 by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behavior was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world six-speed sequential paddle transmission is established by a registered source.

claims.basis: The registered source establishes the real-world identity and transmission, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.
The transmission engineer specifies a paddle-shifted semi-automatic sequential six-speed transaxle; the live drive confirmed six paddle gears and clutch-free move-off.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

notes: The wheel-rim shape was originally recorded as "gt-style". The separate "gt-style", "formula" and "prototype" values described the same rim: molded grips at 9 and 3 with a control face between them, usually carrying a display and rev lights. They are merged into "gt-formula". The rim was not observed again and nothing about the observation changed.
